column1: # .github/required-contexts.tsv
# The branch-protection required-status-check contexts for `main`, and the workflow
# job backing each one. Read by the `required-unfiltered` fence in security-scan.yml,
# which asserts that no workflow listed here can be skipped — because a skipped
# workflow's required context hangs Pending forever and deadlocks the PR.
# FORMAT (tab-separated, 3 fields):  <workflow file>  <job id>  <context name>
# The context name is the job's `name:` — that is the string branch protection
# matches on. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored.
# ⚠ THIS FILE'S KNOWN BLIND SPOT — read before trusting it.
#   This is a MANIFEST, not a mirror. Nothing mechanically proves it matches the
#   actual branch-protection configuration, because reading branch protection
#   requires repo-ADMIN scope and CI's `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot do it (the read is
#   `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches/main/protection`; the token 404s on it). So:
#     - An entry listed here that is NOT actually required → the fence over-enforces.
#       Harmless: it holds an unfiltered workflow unfiltered.
#     - A context actually required that is MISSING here → the fence under-enforces,
#       silently. THAT is the live gap. A newly-required path-filtered workflow would
#       deadlock PRs with nothing having warned.
#   The gap is accepted deliberately rather than closed with a PAT: a token with
#   admin scope in CI would put a production-reaching credential in the CI secret
#   store, which collides head-on with the secrets-manifest CI/production
#   non-overlap commitment that `secrets-nonoverlap` exists to enforce. Trading a
#   documented manifest-sync gap for a hole in the non-overlap posture is a bad
#   trade. (Considered and rejected 2026-08-10, DevOps → F/CTO.)
#   THE COMPENSATING CONTROL IS A HUMAN STEP, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: whenever a
#   context is added to or removed from branch protection, update this file in the
#   same change. Verify with:
#     gh api repos/richmosko/mosko-fintech/branches/main/protection \
#       --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts[]' | sort > /tmp/actual
#     grep -v '^#' .github/required-contexts.tsv | grep -v '^$' \
#       | cut -f3 | sort > /tmp/manifest
#     diff /tmp/actual /tmp/manifest && echo "IN SYNC"
#   That command needs admin scope, so it is run by the F/CTO, not by CI. Run it at
#   every promotion. Do not assume this file is current because CI is green — CI
#   green says only that what IS listed here is unfiltered.

# The fence that enforces this file, listed in it deliberately. If
# `required-unfiltered` is not itself a required context, someone can break it and
# merge anyway — and the failure is quiet, because a broken guard looks exactly like
# a satisfied one. It is self-consistent to list: security-scan.yml carries no
# `paths:` filter and this job carries no `if:`, so it checks itself and passes.
# ⚠ It is NOT yet in branch protection — promoting it is an F/CTO action, and this
# line over-enforces (the harmless direction) until then.
security-scan.yml

column1: # --- NOT listed, and why ---
# etl-ci.yml (unit, pgtest) and web-tests.yml (web-app, dependency-audit) are still
# path-filtered and still advisory. They are candidates for a SECOND batch after this
# one lands and one clean doc-PR cycle is observed. Do not add them here until they
# are de-filtered — listing a filtered workflow makes this fence go red, which is the
# correct fail-closed direction but is not a useful way to discover the intent.
# scheduled-dep-audit.yml has no PR trigger at all (schedule + workflow_dispatch), so
# it can never report a PR check and can never be a required context. Its PR-visible
# proxy is the `scheduled-audit-liveness` job in security-scan.yml, which is not yet
